extracted.intended_audience: state environmental agencies (ODEQ), regulated facilities subject to CISWI, tribal governments, and public commenters/stakeholders
extracted.subtask_description: EPA proposed-rule guidance and evaluation criteria for approving a state's CAA section 111(d)/129 plan for Commercial and Industrial Solid Waste Incineration (CISWI) units, including required plan contents, applicability, procedural rules, and public-comment instructions. Focused on Oklahoma's submitted plan but cites general regulatory requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: EPA approval standard for 111(d)/129 submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the CAA, the Administrator is required to approve a CAA section 111(d)/129 submission that complies with the provisions of the Act and applicable Federal regulations (42 U.S.C. 7411(d); 42 U.S.C. 7429; 40 CFR part 60, subparts B and DDDD; and 40 CFR part 62, subpart A).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA's role is to approve state choices provided they meet the criteria of the Act and implementing regulations; this action proposes to approve state law as meeting Federal requirements and does not impose additional requirements beyond those imposed by state law.

rubrics_metrics.name: State plan: inventory of affected CISWI
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 60.2515 requires an inventory of affected CISWI, including those that have ceased operation but have not been dismantled.

rubrics_metrics.name: State plan: inventory of emissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 60.2515 requires an inventory of emissions from affected CISWI in the State.

rubrics_metrics.name: State plan: compliance schedules
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 60.2515 requires compliance schedules for each affected CISWI.

rubrics_metrics.name: State plan: emission limitations and operational controls
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 60.2515 requires emission limitations, operator training and qualification requirements, a waste management plan, and operating limits for affected CISWIs that are at least as protective as the emission guidelines contained in this subpart.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the state deviates from the format/content of the EG, the state plan must demonstrate that it is at least as protective as the CISWI EG.

rubrics_metrics.name: State plan: performance testing, recordkeeping, and reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 60.2515 requires performance testing, recordkeeping, and reporting requirements to be included in the state plan.

rubrics_metrics.name: State plan: public hearing documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 60.2515 requires certification that the hearing on the state plan was held, a list of witnesses and their organizational affiliations, if any, appearing at the hearing, and a brief written summary of each presentation or written submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: State plan: progress reports to EPA
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 60.2515 requires provision for State progress reports to EPA.

rubrics_metrics.name: State plan: enforceable State mechanisms
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 60.2515 requires identification of enforceable State mechanisms that the State selected for implementing the emission guidelines of this subpart.

rubrics_metrics.name: State plan: demonstration of legal authority
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 60.2515 requires demonstration of the state's legal authority to carry out sections 111(d) and 129 in the state plan.

rubrics_metrics.name: State plan must be at least as protective and follow procedural regs
rubrics_metrics.description: The state plan must demonstrate that it is at least as protective as the CISWI EG if it deviates from the format and content of the EG in 40 CFR part 60, subpart DDDD; the state plan must also follow the requirements of 40 CFR part 60, subpart B.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA's Technical Support Document (TSD) in the docket contains detailed rationale showing how a plan meets these requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Negative declaration option (no designated facilities)
rubrics_metrics.description: 40 CFR 60.23(b) and 40 CFR 62.06 provide that if there are no designated facilities of the designated pollutant(s) in the state, the state may submit a letter of certification to that effect (i.e., negative declaration) in lieu of a plan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The negative declaration exempts the state from the requirements of subpart B that require the submittal of a CAA section 111(d)/129 plan.

rubrics_metrics.name: CISWI EG pollutant numerical emissions requirements (CAA sec.129)
rubrics_metrics.description: Under CAA section 129, NSPS and EG must contain numerical emissions limitations for particulate matter, opacity (as appropriate), sulfur dioxide, hydrogen chloride, oxides of nitrogen, carbon monoxide, lead, cadmium, mercury, and dioxins and dibenzofurans.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability of CISWI EG (which facilities are 'designated facilities')
rubrics_metrics.description: As provided by 40 CFR 60.2505, the designated facilities to which the CISWI EG apply are CISWI and air curtain incinerators (ACI) that commenced construction on or before June 4, 2010, or for which modification or reconstruction was commenced on or before August 7, 2013, with limited exceptions as provided under 40 CFR 60.2555.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certain ACIs that may not fit the definition of a 'CISWI' under the CISWI EG are addressed at 40 CFR 60.2875.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incorporation by reference requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Inclusion in a final rule of regulatory text that incorporates by reference revisions to state regulations must comply with 1 CFR 51.5.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA proposes to make these documents generally available electronically through regulations.gov and provides contact info for obtaining incorporated documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public comment submission rules and restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Submit comments identified by Docket No. EPA-R06-OAR-2020-0610 at regulations.gov or via the provided email; follow online instructions. Once submitted, comments cannot be edited or removed. EPA may publish any comment received to its public docket. Do not submit electronically any information you consider to be Confidential Business Information (CBI) or other information whose disclosure is restricted by statute. Multimedia submissions must be accompanied by a written comment (the written comment is the official comment).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA will generally not consider comments or comment contents located outside of the primary submission (i.e., on the web, cloud, or other file sharing system). See EPA public comment policy at https://www.epa.gov/dockets/commenting-epa-dockets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public comment close date
rubrics_metrics.description: Written comments must be received on or before August 19, 2024.

rubrics_metrics.name: Docket access and limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: The index to the docket for this action is available electronically at regulations.gov. While all documents in the docket are listed in the index, some information may not be publicly available due to docket file size restrictions or content (e.g., CBI).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contact the EPA person listed in the FOR FURTHER INFORMATION CONTACT section for alternative access to material indexed but not provided in the docket.

rubrics_metrics.name: Environmental Justice screening: appropriate use and limitations of EJSCREEN
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA conducted screening analyses using EJSCREEN, an environmental justice mapping and screening tool that provides a nationally consistent dataset and approach for combining various environmental and demographic indicators. EJSCREEN presents indicators at a Census block group (CBG) level or a larger user-specified 'buffer' area.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EJSCREEN is not a tool for performing in-depth risk analysis but is a screening tool subject to uncertainty (monitoring data limitations, ACS sampling error). EPA summarized EJSCREEN data within larger buffer areas for the affected sources; the EJ analysis is provided for informational transparency and not as a basis of the proposed action.

rubrics_metrics.name: EJ indicators and demographic metrics presented
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA's EJSCREEN reports include pollution burden indicators (annual PM2.5, ozone, traffic proximity and volume score, percent pre-1960 housing [lead paint indicator], proximity scores to Superfund, RMP, hazardous waste facilities) and demographic indicators (percent low-income, people of color, linguistic isolation, education, percent under 5, percent over 64).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA presented results as percentiles within the U.S. and used ~3-mile buffer areas around the affected incinerator for summary reporting; full EJSCREEN reports are in the docket.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tribal/Indian country scope under SAFETEA
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA's approval under SAFETEA (section 10211(a)) to allow Oklahoma to administer approved state environmental regulatory programs in certain areas of Indian country is acknowledged; the proposed approval will apply to all Indian country within Oklahoma other than specified excluded Indian country lands (certain Indian allotments, lands held in trust on behalf of an individual Indian or Tribe, and certain tribal fee lands acquired via treaty where not allotted).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA notes the October 1, 2020 SAFETEA approval is under review and subject to potential withdrawal/reconsideration; changes to that approval could affect the geographic scope before finalization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory and Executive Order applicability determinations (procedural review tests)
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA assesses applicability of various statutes and Executive Orders in its review: Executive Order 12866 (significant regulatory action), Paperwork Reduction Act (information collection burden), Regulatory Flexibility Act (economic impact on small entities), Unfunded Mandates Reform Act (unfunded mandates), Executive Order 13132 (federalism), Executive Order 13175 (tribal consultation), Executive Order 13045 (children's health/safety risks), Executive Order 13211 (energy impacts), National Technology Transfer and Advancement Act (technical standards), and Executive Order 12898 (environmental justice).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For this proposed action EPA determined: not a significant regulatory action under EO12866; no PRA information collection burden; certified no significant economic impact under RFA; no unfunded mandate under UMRA; no federalism implications; tribal implications addressed and consultation offered where applicable; not subject to EO13045 or EO13211; NTTAA not applicable because inconsistent with CAA; EO12898: EPA performed EJ analysis for informational purposes but the action is expected to have neutral or beneficial impacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance expectation: EG yields emission reductions and health benefits
rubrics_metrics.description: CISWI EG requirements result in emission reductions for specified pollutants (PM, SO2, HCl, NOX, CO, Pb, Cd, Hg, and dioxins/furans) and provide opacity limits; information on emissions, relationship to health impacts, and estimated benefits can be found in the referenced Federal Register document and Regulatory Impact Analysis.
